artifacts.notes: Extent as the retrieving lane measured it: Complete file for McLean v. Arkansas Board of Education as CAP holds it, 529 F. Supp. 1249-1268, whole memorandum opinion with all footnotes, star markers *1250 through *1268 present plus a repeated *1251 and *1255 at the end of the file. TWO CAUTIONS FROM THE RETRIEVING LANE. The reporter or the transcription gives a publisher as 'Zonderman Publishing House' where the publisher of the title is Zondervan, so that name must not be reproduced without checking. And the file repeats star markers *1251 and *1255 at its end. The textbook the court quotes is in copyright and only the court's own brief quotation of it is usable.
artifacts.rights_basis: A judicial opinion of a court of the United States and its official reporter carry no copyright: under the government edicts doctrine the works of judges in their judicial capacity are not copyrightable, and the retrieving research lane of run efff3a6f73c1f451 recorded the same finding for every member of this set, in the form 'US court opinions and official reporters; public domain'. The file is the reporter's text with the Caselaw Access Project's minimal star-pagination markup and nothing else -- no navigation, no styling, no site apparatus. The bytes are retained at 0.12 MB so that a reader with no network can reopen the sentence a claim quotes; guidance/sources.md makes that the default and names size as the only other exemption, which a file this small cannot reach. BOUND, stated rather than assumed: the Caselaw Access Project's own terms for its transcriptions were not read by the retrieving lane and were not read here, so the basis above is the opinion's own status in law and not a grant by that project.
